stem: A trend shows repeated lights-on temperature spikes even though the 24-hour average is within range. What belongs in the handoff?
choices: Report only the acceptable 24-hour average because it is the formal summary metric.
Report a confirmed HVAC fault because repeated lights-on spikes indicate equipment failure.
Omit the pattern because an average within range shows the room met the environmental requirement overall.

Report the repeated lights-on spike pattern with timing and location, relevant checks or comparisons, escalation status, and the fact that root cause remains unresolved if it has not been established.
rationale: A 24-hour average can hide repeated short excursions that may matter operationally. The handoff should preserve the recurring spike pattern and its timing rather than letting the average erase it. Technician I should also separate observation from diagnosis: the pattern can justify escalation without proving an HVAC fault.
